requirements.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared, writable directory on node1
requirements.summary: Directory created with mode 1777, root:root ownership, world-writable, confirmed via stat before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users in /srv/drop
requirements.summary: Sticky bit behaviorally verified: dropuser2 was denied ('Operation not permitted') when attempting to delete dropuser1's file, while each owner could delete their own file. Re-verified post-reboot with a fresh user pair (verifyA/verifyB) with identical results.

overall_summary: The executor correctly configured /srv/drop as mode 1777 (world-writable with sticky bit) owned by root:root, and directly demonstrated via a two-user behavioral test both before and after a full node restart that non-owners cannot delete other users' files while owners can. The mandatory single-node restart protocol was also completed with a clear pre-restart boot identity (dfdea52d...), restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity (5b01788d...), and confirmed persistence/recovery of both the directory configuration and sticky-bit behavior - corroborated independently by the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. All test users and files were cleaned up.
limitations: The before_prepare and after_prepare snapshots are aliased (prepare disabled), so no independent preparer-vs-executor baseline separation was possible beyond the fixed diff already computed.
A small transient artifact (/tmp/reboot.log) from the backgrounded shutdown command was left in place; low-risk and does not affect functional outcomes.
No group-based or ACL alternative was tested since sticky bit alone was sufficient and matches the stated requirement; this is not a deficiency, just noting the single implementation path verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Test users (dropuser1, dropuser2, verifyA, verifyB) were created for behavioral verification, a reasonable and necessary step to demonstrate the sticky-bit outcome, and all were fully cleaned up (final getent checks show no matches). Test files in /srv/drop were also removed. One minor inefficiency: the first userdel attempt (cmd-1828f37360c64b6d) failed because of lingering systemd --user sessions, requiring a follow-up pkill+userdel (cmd-58b6c75fdb694c42) to complete cleanup - this is a corrective action, not an unnecessary mutation, so not penalized. The mandatory node restart (cmd-fcc3d735719946e0) is an expected, in-scope action for the fixed restart-evidence protocol, not task-unrelated. /tmp/reboot.log is a transient artifact of the backgrounded shutdown command and is low-risk residue, not explicitly cleaned up, which is the only minor hygiene deduction.
